brief: A checklist for shipping something you will not be embarrassed by

slots.eyebrow: On the hour before you send it
slots.standfirst: Six passes over a finished piece of work, in the order that finds the most for the least effort.
slots.item1: The errors that survive every earlier round because nobody was looking for them
slots.item2: About forty minutes, and the version of you that wanted to be finished
slots.coverNote: The last pass is the one people skip, and it is the one that matters

slots.titleLine1: Start from the top, as a stranger.
slots.body: Not scanning for the bits you were worried about — reading the whole thing in order, the way somebody who has never seen it will. Almost every serious problem is visible in the first ninety seconds to anybody but you.
slots.v1: Stopping to fix puts you back inside the work and ends the cold read.
slots.v2: A list of marks is worth more than three repairs and a lost thread.
slots.v3: Every place you reread a line is a place somebody else stops entirely.
slots.v4: The opening is written first and revised least, which is the wrong way round.

slots.titleLine1: Every number has a source or it goes.
slots.body: Figures acquire confidence by being repeated, including by you, and the one that turns out to be wrong is always the one nobody could remember the origin of. If you cannot find where it came from in a minute, the honest move is to delete it.
slots.v1: To the actual source, not to the place you saw it quoted.
slots.v2: A true figure from four years ago is a false claim about now.
slots.v3: Numbers used for texture rather than argument are pure risk.
slots.v4: Attribution converts a claim you are defending into one you are reporting.

slots.titleLine1: Remove ten per cent after you finish.
slots.body: Not a rewrite — a removal pass, made when the work is already done and you are least willing to do it. The tenth that goes is almost never load-bearing, and taking it out is the cheapest quality improvement available at that stage.
slots.v1: A paragraph, a section, a slide. Trimming words tightens without shortening.
slots.v2: The part you are proudest of is usually the part serving you.
slots.v3: Somewhere else. Deleting is much easier when it is not destroying.
slots.v4: If nothing is missing, the cut was correct and you can go further.

slots.titleLine1: Do the thing you are asking for.
slots.body: Follow your own instruction end to end, exactly as written, without the knowledge you have and they do not. Roughly half the time it does not work, and the failure is always in a step you considered too obvious to write down.
slots.v1: The actual link, the actual file, on the machine somebody else has.
slots.v2: Where you had to improvise is exactly where the instruction is missing.
slots.v3: If it takes twice as long as you claimed, say the real number.
slots.v4: Ten minutes of somebody else trying beats an hour of you checking.

slots.titleLine1: The last thing they see is the first thing they judge.
slots.body: Titles, file names, the preview line, the opening sentence — the parts made last, in a hurry, after the real work was finished. They carry a disproportionate share of the impression, and they are the cheapest things in the whole piece to improve.
slots.v1: You only know what the thing is once it exists.
slots.v2: Somebody will see the name before they see anything inside it.
slots.v3: The first eighty characters are doing more work than page two.
slots.v4: Most people will meet this as a thumbnail and a line of text.

slots.body: Every item here has a stopping point, and past it more checking produces changes rather than improvements. The signal is simple: when a pass finds only things you could argue either way, you are no longer editing, you are delaying.
slots.v1: A pass that finds nothing real is the last pass, by definition.
slots.v2: Decide how many passes before you start. Then do exactly that many.
slots.v3: Changing something back is the clearest evidence you are done.
slots.v4: The last hour improves almost nothing and costs the whole afternoon.

slots.eyebrow: On the thing you are about to send
slots.titleLine1: Read it cold, then cut a tenth.
slots.body: Two passes, about forty minutes between them. They catch more than the other four put together, and neither of them requires anybody else.
slots.closingLine: Everything on this list is cheaper than the conversation about why it went out wrong.
